# Mission Control v2.1.0 — Production Remote Operations Platform

Mission Control has evolved from a CRUD application into a production-ready IT Operations Platform.

Version 2.1.0 delivers a complete Remote Operations module alongside a modern Windows Admin Center-inspired interface — providing a solid foundation for enterprise infrastructure management.

---

## Highlights

### Remote Operations

- Real SSH command execution via Paramiko
- Real WinRM command execution via pywinrm
- Remote host management with full CRUD
- Secure credential management with encrypted vault
- Command history with execution source tracking
- Reusable command templates with category and protocol tagging
- Bulk command execution across multiple hosts simultaneously
- Scheduled commands with cron-based triggering and run-now capability
- Remote file transfer (upload, download, base64-encoded)
- Remote file browser with directory listing, creation, and deletion
- Session metrics tracking (active sessions, command counts, latency)
- Full audit logging across all remote operations

### Security

- Fernet-encrypted credential vault (AES-128-CBC at rest)
- Sensitive fields never exposed through the API layer
- Secure logging — passwords and keys are never written to logs
- Provider isolation architecture separating auth from execution

### User Interface

- Windows Admin Center-inspired layout with persistent sidebar
- Collapsible navigation groups (Dashboard, Infrastructure, Remote Operations, Settings)
- Top bar with breadcrumb navigation and route labels
- Status bar with live clock and connection info
- Dashboard redesign with stat cards, system gauges, health badges, and quick actions
- Dedicated infrastructure pages (Overview, System, Docker, Git, Health)
- Remote Operations workspace (Hosts, Credentials, Execute, History, Files)
- Modern reusable component library (DataTable, EmptyState, PageHeader, SearchInput, StatusBadge)
- Improved user experience across all pages

### Backend Architecture

- FastAPI with async support
- SQLAlchemy ORM with full model layer
- PostgreSQL with Alembic migrations (10 models, 9 migration scripts)
- Repository pattern for clean data access
- Service layer separating business logic from routing
- Provider architecture (Strategy pattern) with factory singletons
- Pydantic request/response schemas with validation
- Dependency injection via FastAPI `Depends()`

### Infrastructure Monitoring

- Docker container status and statistics
- Git repository health (branch, commits, working tree)
- System health overview (hostname, OS, CPU, memory, disk)
- Database health checks
- Redis health checks
- Dashboard metrics aggregation

### Quality

- 307 backend tests passing (API integration, repositories, services, providers)
- Ruff linting validated
- TypeScript strict mode enforced
- Production build verified (223 kB JS, 28 kB CSS)
- Docker deployment verified

## Architecture

Mission Control follows a layered architecture:

```
React Frontend
      ↓
   REST API
      ↓
 Service Layer
      ↓
Provider Layer
      ↓
 Repositories
      ↓
Database / Infrastructure Providers
```

**Infrastructure providers currently include:**

- Docker
- Git
- System
- Health
- SSH
- WinRM

This architecture allows future integrations to plug in without modifying the dashboard or existing providers.
